Change c0136. Location: 1818 Vol. I, Ch. VI; 1831 Ch. VII.

Context before (unchanged): When she again lived, it was only to weep and sigh.

1818 text: She told me, that that same evening William had teazed her to let him wear a very valuable miniature that she possessed of your mother.

1831 text: She told me, that that same evening William had teased her to let him wear a very valuable miniature that she possessed of your mother.

Diff: She told me, that that same evening William had [-teazed-] {+teased+} her to let him wear a very valuable miniature that she possessed of your mother.

Context after (unchanged): This picture is gone, and was doubtless the temptation which urged the murderer to the deed.

result.rationale: The only change is teazed to teased, a regularization of the past-tense spelling with no change in wording or meaning in the sentence about William and the miniature.
